identity.definition: Polydeoxyribonucleotide: preparations made from DNA fragments. Source, fragment-size profile, formulation, and delivery route can differ materially between products and studies.
identity.source_type: DNA-fragment preparation; animal-derived and plant-described variants exist

preferred: Use the exact ingredient-list wording photographed on the product
label_terms.rule: Treat these as possible market or label terms, not automatic synonyms. Never infer source, fragment size, concentration, or equivalence from the front label alone.

identity_boundaries: PDRN and PN are not interchangeable by default.
Evidence from injection does not transfer automatically to an intact-skin topical serum.
Evidence for one defined preparation such as PDRN-850K does not prove every product marketed as PDRN.
Salmon-derived is common in studied preparations, but not every marketed PDRN product should be called salmon DNA without product-specific evidence.

visual_system.actor: Short DNA-fragment ribbons or paired nucleotide segments, never a giant rotating genome helix.
visual_system.tactile_signature: Nearly clear, faintly opalescent serum with precise glass and restrained clinical light.
motion_grammar: Fragment first: show short segments assembling into a dossier, not a spinning hero helix.
Use route transitions as the main explanatory motion: bottle, skin surface, needle/clinic are separate states.
Let evidence markers land after the route and study population are visible.

avoid: claiming the liquid proves purity or a biological effect

assets.notes: New pilot asset. Fixed cream background; not a transparent cutout.

components.purpose: Name the ingredient while making source, preparation, and route variables visible.
Provide ingredient recognition without the generic spinning-helix cliché.

components.type: topical versus procedure versus injected comparison
components.purpose: Prevent route borrowing, the biggest accuracy risk in PDRN content.
Show split-face study design after its current legacy source mapping is replaced with a traceable publication.
Use only after replacing old internal PDRN source IDs with traceable citations.

evidence_records.claim: In a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial, intramuscular and perilesional PDRN improved healing outcomes in people with hard-to-heal diabetic foot ulcers.
evidence_records.scope: diabetic foot ulcers; 216 randomized; 192 completed; eight weeks
limits: does not establish benefits for intact-skin topical products

citation.title: The effect of PDRN, an adenosine receptor A2A agonist, on the healing of chronic diabetic foot ulcers: results of a clinical trial

evidence_records.claim: A randomized double-blind split-face study found greater 28-day improvements in several periocular measurements with a specific 0.1% PDRN-850K eye cream than with an identically based 0.1% retinol eye cream.
evidence_records.scope: 31 healthy Chinese women aged 35–55; one PDRN-850K eye cream; 28 days
limits: single defined preparation and eye-cream formula
early changes may partly reflect hydration or plumping
not evidence for every PDRN product

citation.title: Topical medium-length PDRN enhances dermal extracellular matrix repair in photodamaged skin via PI3K–Akt/TGF-β–regulated pathways

evidence_records.claim: The same PDRN-850K paper reported pathway and extracellular-matrix findings in cultured fibroblasts and UV-damaged ex vivo skin models.
evidence_records.route: cell, reconstructed-skin, ex vivo, and exploratory penetration models
limits: laboratory mechanism is not a consumer outcome
do not convert pathway activation into instant repair language
not a generic A2A-receptor proof card

citation.title: Topical medium-length PDRN enhances dermal extracellular matrix repair in photodamaged skin via PI3K–Akt/TGF-β–regulated pathways

evidence_records.claim: Evidence for one topical PDRN preparation cannot be generalized to products with unknown source, size distribution, concentration, or vehicle.
limits: use as an editorial evidence boundary, not as proof that all other products fail

citation.title: Scope and limitations stated by Ye et al.

safe_default: PDRN refers to DNA-fragment preparations, but products can differ in source, fragment profile, formulation, and route.
Injected medical evidence and topical cosmetic evidence must be shown separately.
One small 2026 trial provides promising evidence for one defined topical eye cream, not the whole category.
Read the exact label rather than relying on a large PDRN claim on the front of the package.
requires_context: Salmon DNA — use only when the actual studied preparation or product source is documented.
Wound healing — state diabetic foot ulcer, injection route, and medical setting.
Wrinkle or dermal improvement — state PDRN-850K, 0.1% eye cream, n=31, 28 days, retinol comparator, and limitations.
Mechanism language — attach it to the defined preparation and label it cell or ex vivo evidence.

story_slots.purpose: Open on the category tension: medical evidence versus cosmetic product.
Define PDRN and teach label ambiguity.
avoid: equating PDRN, PN, Hydrolyzed DNA, and Sodium DNA automatically

story_slots.purpose: Make the delivery route visible before discussing evidence.
avoid: borrowing injection results for a topical bottle

story_slots.purpose: Present the strongest currently located topical human evidence with limitations.
Use mechanism only as a clearly labeled model or laboratory finding.

format_input.boundary_card: Route, preparation, and formula matter: injection evidence is not serum evidence.
